g.text: The QoS ladder: context isolation + a 25–35% MPS SM cap returns a 100 Hz loop to 0 drops — but no step moves the 172 GB/s CPU-memory floor
One Thor GPU, π0.5 VLA + 100 Hz WBC loop (10 ms deadline). Each step adds discipline; QoS does not add capacity, it assigns the penalty. Values from the L4 campaign [L4].

g.text: — step height ≈ QoS delivered to the WBC loop (higher = better isolation)
— red = loop broken · green = loop meets 10 ms deadline (0% drop) · grey dashed = deferred/not-a-lever
— thick red dashed line = the ~172 GB/s CPU-memory floor (precision- and cap-invariant)
Takeaway: context isolation is the dominant lever; the SM cap is the finisher (closes the last ~10×, 4.9%->0%). QoS assigns the penalty, it does not add capacity [L4].

Sources (from constants.json / notes, not retyped): [L4] L4-scheduling-ladder KEY-LEARNINGS — shared_context_wbc_penalty (64×, 51%), separate_context_wbc_p99 (π0.5 17 ms/4.9%, GR00T 14.3 ms), plain MPS (61 ms/25%), mps_cap_wbc_p99 (cap25 7.5, cap35 9.1/8.9 ms, 0% drop), mps_cap_vla_rate_retained (0.72–0.90), cpu_memory_load_floor (172 GB/s), MIG deferred. WBC solo p99 41.6 µs (Thor) [B.8].
